questions.scenario: Your friends want to learn how to play a very complicated new video game. How do you teach them?

options.text: I sit with them and explain the rules step-by-step like a class.
I make a quick screen-recording video explaining the controls.
I teach them psychological tricks and strategies to defeat the opponents.
I hold their hand, play the first few levels with them patiently, and cheer them on.
I write a detailed, easy-to-read manual or cheat sheet with diagrams for them to follow.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were asked to give a presentation to 100 people, what would be your ideal setup?

options.text: A big classroom with a whiteboard and a marker in my hand.
A studio with a green screen, good lighting, and cool animations.
A premium conference room where I can walk around and motivate people.
A quiet, comfortable room where I can sit in a circle and talk face-to-face.
I'd rather stay behind the scenes, designing the ultimate slide deck or workbook for the speaker.
None of these.

questions.scenario: A junior student is crying because they failed a math test. What is your reaction?

options.text: I take their notebook and teach them the formulas they got wrong.
I send them a link to a fun YouTube video that explains the topic easily.
I give them a strong motivational speech to build their lost confidence.
I sit quietly with them until they stop crying, and slowly remove their fear of math.
I analyze the test paper to see if the questions were poorly worded and redesign a better practice test for them.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you had to start your own YouTube channel, what would the videos be about?

options.text: Deep, detailed lectures on History, Science, or Geography.
Fast-paced, 60-second animated shorts sharing amazing facts.
Personality development, communication skills, and how to look confident.
Sign language, mental health awareness, and helping disabled kids.
Reviewing different study methods, analyzing textbooks, and explaining how the brain learns best.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of 'superpower' fits your personality the best?

options.text: Discipline: I can make a noisy room pin-drop silent just by looking.
Broadcast: I can instantly beam my thoughts into millions of screens.
Charisma: I can make anyone feel like a superhero instantly.
Telepathy: I can understand the feelings of people who cannot speak.
Structure: I can organize a million pages of chaotic information into one perfect, easy-to-understand map.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You are organizing a summer camp. Which activity do you choose to lead?

options.text: The daily quiz and general knowledge competition.
The photography and video-editing workshop.
The leadership and public speaking debates.
The art therapy class for kids who are very shy or anxious.
Designing the entire camp's daily schedule, rules, and learning materials behind the scenes.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every teaching job has a 'boring' part. Which of these can you tolerate easily?

options.text: Checking 100 identical exam papers with a red pen.
Sitting alone for 5 hours editing a 10-minute video.
Listening to grown adults complain about their job stress.
Repeating the exact same simple word 50 times with a smile.
Reading 50 different heavy textbooks just to write one perfect, error-free chapter.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were a guide in a historical museum, what would be your style?

options.text: Gathering 40 students and explaining the exact historical dates loudly.
Creating an interactive audio-guide app for visitors to scan and listen.
Training the other junior guides on how to speak confidently.
Helping a blind or deaf visitor experience the museum through touch.
I wouldn't guide; I'd be the one researching and writing the detailed information plaques for the exhibits.
None of these.

questions.scenario: During a group project, there is one member who is very weak and confused. You will...

options.text: Give them a simple textbook and tell them exactly what to read.
Make a WhatsApp group and send them voice notes and links to understand.
Coach them on just how to present the project so they look confident.
Do the work alongside them at their slow pace so they don't feel left out.
Break the project down into a clear, step-by-step checklist so they know exactly what to do without feeling overwhelmed.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In your friend circle, what title describes you the best?

options.text: The Professor (Always knows the facts).
The Creator (Always using tech to explain things).
The Coach (Always hyping people up).
The Nurturer (Always patient and kind).
The Architect (Always structuring, planning, and organizing information).
None of these.
